activity.notes: Amanishakheto is securely attested as a ruling Meroitic queen. Her absolute chronology near the BCE/CE transition is disputed: the British Museum gives 10–1 BCE, while the 2021 UCLA Encyclopedia of Egyptology places her around the beginning of the first century CE after Amanirenas. ATLAS therefore uses a deliberately broad c.10 BCE–c.1 CE bracket with approximate boundaries rather than presenting either chronology as exact. 'Candace' is a Latinized form of the title Kandake, not part of her personal name.

sources.title: Meroe and Egypt — UCLA Encyclopedia of Egyptology (Josefine Kuckertz, 2021)
sources.citation_text: Kuckertz places the ruling queen Amanishakheto around the beginning of the first century CE as successor to Amanirenas and notes that royal succession around the BCE/CE transition remains controversial.

sources.title: Amanishakheto — British Museum Collections Online
sources.citation_text: The British Museum identifies Amanishakheto as a Meroitic female ruler and gives the traditional reign dating 10 BC–1 BC.
